coverage_note: Long English stretches (collocation meta talk 12:00-13:30, hear vs listen 31:00-34:00, rule-adding 22:40-23:30). Latin-transliterated Medi turns 10:29-11:57, 13:29-27:39, 49:00-54:00. [foreign language] holes at 28:18, 29:37, 30:11, 31:07-33:04 (اسمعيني / اسمع له attempts unreadable). 09:52 and 10:05-10:11 engine garbage (soup). 47:06 'عمان ما را' = kaman marra (he answered 'one more time'), not Amman. 58:01 / 59:19 'Ramallah?' = he asked what she said. 10:47 'ana rah kunet' was a question about order, not counted. 45:24 'أي سهل؟' = he misheard her هاي سهلة, not scored.

rows.why: Engine wrote حليت بوجه for 7al2i + a hurt verb; her chat has beywajje3 (it hurts) while his form sounds like bowja3 (I hurt); chat alone is not a correction, so let pass.

rows.medi_said: بعدت، uh، امبارح مع بنات أخوي.
rows.chat: ana a3adet mbaare7 shwai ma3 banaat a5uy
rows.why: He said بعدت (I went away); she asked back what his word was and he switched to قعدت (I sat / stayed) - may be the engine on ب/ق.
rows.english: Yesterday I sat with my brother's daughters.

rows.amal_said: شغل؟ Who؟ My work؟ أوكي، ممتاز.
rows.chat: heyye saarat a7san u rej3at 3ala shu8ulha
rows.why: He put 'your' on work for his fiancee; she asked 'my work?' and he fixed to شغلها.
rows.english: She went back to her work.

rows.why: Today (10-12) is Monday; he said Tuesday and she said No.

rows.medi_said: No، يوم ال-- oh، يوم الثنتين.
rows.why: He gave the feminine 'two' as the day name; she said No and gave tenain.

rows.amal_said: على. / الـ، على الـ سبعة ونص.
rows.why: Clock time needs el-; she prompted 'الـ' and gave على السبعة ونص, he repeated it.

rows.medi_said: Sihit tasah. Um, lama, uh, lama tisah.
rows.amal_said: This because you said بتفكري. Mm-hmm. تصحي.
rows.chat: shu awal ishi betfakkr fiyyo lamma tes7i
rows.why: He asked her with feminine bitfikri then masculine tisah; she pointed at بتفكري and gave the feminine تصحي.

rows.medi_said: awwal ishi ana bitfikri feel subah. / Ba fakri feel s--
rows.chat: awal ishi ana bafakker fiyyo el-subu7
rows.why: Answering about himself he used the you(f) form; she said 'I think' and gave بفكر.
rows.english: The first thing I think about in the morning.

rows.amal_said: About. ... فيه، فيه الصبح. You need two فيهs.
rows.chat: awal ishi ana bafakker fiyyo el-subu7
rows.why: Object awwal ishi was fronted so the preposition needs the pointer ending fiyyo; she named it ('refer it back to أول إشي').
rows.english: I think about it in the morning.

rows.why: He first said futoor, then added el-; she recast without el-.

rows.medi_said: So ba-, uh, ba- baul is speak.
rows.why: He named بقول (say) as 'speak'; she said no, just بحكي.

rows.amal_said: It is عن، بس where do I put it؟ ... the order is wrong.
rows.why: Preposition left dangling at the end; she said the order is wrong and he moved عن to the front.

rows.amal_said: بس بتفكري takes what؟ ... No, we don't need عن ... فيه شو بتفكري؟
rows.why: For 'thinking about' he used عن; she asked what بتفكري takes and gave في شو بتفكري (engine wrote bitihki, her echo is بتفكري).
Asking 'do you know' he used the I-form ba3ref; she gave بتعرف and he moved to bit3arfi.
rows.english: Do you know how to play this game?

rows.amal_said: No be. ... I hear be. تلعب.
rows.why: Second verb after بتعرفي drops b-; she said 'No be' three times and gave تلعب.
He meant 'I heard' but used the present; she said 'I heard' and he switched to سمعت.
Plain present needs b-; her chat writes bey5awwef, she voiced nothing.

rows.amal_said: This. ... ستنيت ... ate is always past ... ستني is for a girl.
rows.why: He gave a past form for a command to a girl; she explained -eet is past and the command is ستني.

rows.amal_said: No. That's see me. شوفني is see me. Look at me.
rows.why: He used شاف (see) for 'look at'; she said No, that's 'see me'.

rows.amal_said: No. At me. ... At. تطلع علي.
rows.why: طلع takes على; he put the object on the verb; she said No, 'at me', تطلع علي.

rows.amal_said: No. What do I do in questions? ... In questions, what's the order of words؟
rows.why: Preposition must go before شو; she said No and asked about question order, he fixed to على شو بتطلعي.

rows.amal_said: No. Don't look. We're using تتطلع.
rows.why: Again شاف (see) for 'look'; she said No, we're using تتطلع.
Negative command is ma + you-form without b- (her chat ma tet6lla3i); she said Yes.

rows.amal_said: You said ما. ... But there's no ما. Why did you put ما؟
rows.why: 'They are looking at you' is positive; she told him there is no ما.
'at you' needs the you(f) ending; he said 'at me' and she recast عليكي.

rows.chat: ana ba7ebb at6lla3 3ala manzar lama ana akoon fi el-tabi3a
rows.why: Wrong (feminine) form of منظر; she gave منظر and he repeated it.
rows.english: I like to look at the view.

rows.chat: ana ba7ebb at6lla3 3ala manzar lama ana akoon fi el-tabi3a
rows.why: Habitual 'when I am in' needs akoon; she recast أكون في الطبيعة.

rows.amal_said: اشرحيني is like explain me. اشرحيني. So اشرحيلي is.
rows.why: 'to me' goes on li- (shara7 la-); she said اشرحيني means 'explain me' and gave اشرحيلي.
Asked 'invite them' he put 'me' on the verb; she repeated 'Invite them' (right form is my reading from her chat e3zemihom).
Past 'I invited you' has no a- prefix; she recast عزمتك.

rows.medi_said: Katebti wana uh ben alan. / Ashan ben alan.
rows.amal_said: شو يعني we worry؟ You are worried or you worry؟ لا بن-- لا.
rows.why: He used the verb 'we worry' for a state; she asked worried or worry, said لا to بن-, he gave alaneen.
rows.english: My fiancee and I are worried.

rows.why: 3aroos is bride; wedding is 3urs; she gave عرس and later 'say it after me عرس'.

rows.amal_said: بس 300 is more than 10 so ... أشخاص أو شخص. ... 300 شخص.
rows.why: Over 10 takes a singular noun; she named the rule.
Invite to an event is 3azam 3ala (this week's collocation); her chat has 3ala 3urusna, she voiced only the noun fix.

rows.medi_said: arasna ... akthar min sitt, uh, shahar.
rows.amal_said: عرس no. ... We never say it this straightforward.
rows.why: 'Our wedding is in 6+ months' needs ba3ed; she said no and prompted until he offered baad and she said yes.
rows.english: Our wedding is in more than six months.

rows.medi_said: Akthar min sitt ashahar. Sitt shahar.
rows.amal_said: No ستة is no-- less than 10. ... شهر is one month بس ستة is less than 10.
rows.why: 3-10 take a plural; first said sitt shahar at 52:41; she named the rule and he gave shahur.
'My fiancee and I' need the plural adjective; she said 'plural' and he gave mishtahazine (engine for mish jaahzeen).
After jaahzeen (ready to) the verb drops b-; said at 54:59 and 56:17, she recast نصير at 56:18 and he took it.

rows.amal_said: We plan for. ... we plan for it in Arabic.
rows.why: خطط takes la-; she said 'We plan for' and he asked خطط لا عرس, she said yes.
Same slip again after her fix; she prompted 'la?' and he said بنخطط لـ عرس.
He mixed بطلب (request) with بطلع (go out); she said no and later explained.
She asked 'request a day off' as a command; he used the present, she said No, command, and he gave اطلبي.
